AlternateTargets: a step forward atop the pole
advance from the top of the pole
Senses.Explanation: Literally, ‘stepping forward from the pole-top,’ the shortened case label and fixed phrase drawn from ‘atop a hundred-foot pole one must step forward’ (百尺竿頭須進步). The verse says that the person sitting atop the pole, although having gained entry, is not yet real, then gives the step-forward line and ‘the worlds in the ten directions are the whole body.’ Wumen's Barrier titles Case 46 ‘Stepping Forward from the Pole-top’ and frames the question as Shishuang's: ‘atop a hundred-foot pole, how does one step forward?’ Other records ask ‘what is the phrase of stepping forward atop a hundred-foot pole?’ and preserve answers such as ‘the southern continent and the northern continent.’ Later verse commentary explicitly names Old Changsha and also joins the pole-top step with Chaling's donkey-fall story. Thus the ordinary impossibility of stepping beyond a pole's tip becomes a named case, a recurrent public question, and a quoted verse-line. The entry reports those textual relations and does not state what the step is intended to accomplish.
Senses.Note: This is the event/action member of the “hundred-foot pole-top” (百尺竿頭) family, not a second reading of the pole-top location. It remains one sense across title, question, and quotation because each names the same step from the same pole-top image.

Occurrences.Kwic: 竿頭進步石霜和尚云。百尺竿頭如何進步。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wumen's case title is followed by the pole-top question attributed only as Shishuang; the identity is left unresolved.

Occurrences.Kwic: 百尺竿頭坐底人。雖然得入。未為真。百尺竿頭須進步十方世界現全身。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The case preserves the old verse's own gained-entry/not-yet-real contrast and its required step.

Occurrences.Kwic: 百尺竿頭進步時築着磕著自家底老長沙
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Later commentary explicitly associates the pole-top step with Old Changsha.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問如何是百尺竿頭進步底句師云南贍部洲北欝單越
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The fixed phrase is asked as a public question; the record gives the southern and northern continents as the reply.
